newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunmen wound policeman in Algiers - witness.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen wound policeman in Algiers - witness.

text.p: Three gunmen thought to be Moslem guerrillas on Wednesday shot and wounded a policman standing guard near Algiers main railway station, an eyewitness said.
The eyewitness, speaking by telephone from the Algerian capital, said security forces quickly moved into the area and were seen chasing the attackers along the railway lines.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
More than 170 Moslem guerrillas were killed in a security forces offensive in the past four weeks in Algiers and nearby provinces, according to Algerian newspaper reports.

Suspected Moslem guerrillas, in the latest massacre of civilians, slaughtered 33 villagers at the weekend in a night raid in Kerrach hamlet in Blida region, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, Algerian newspapers said on Tuesday.
